title: Revisiting the Hero's Journey Home - solo card-based adventure game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cga1y52KSCk

Prompted by a question in the Dungeon Dive Facebook group, Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to Graham Cranfield's The Hero's Journey Home — a game he loves in play and somehow forgets when listing favourites, exactly as he does with Hand of Fate: Ordeals.

The premise is an inversion: the quest is already won and you are playing the walk home. Which quest you completed sets your budget — the Minotaur pays 19 points to spend assembling a party, and hands you a ball of string that replays a journey card. Adventurers carry passive and active abilities, spellcasters draw their spells at random, and casting is paid for in gold or in hit points, stats doubling as currency being one of his favourite mechanisms anywhere.

The newest expansion adds spellcasting monsters that only cast when their physical attack misses, plus Game Changer cards — a vow of poverty trades away monster rewards for gold in every village and a fourth prayer. There's a lovely aside: the designer posted that expansion to his office before the pandemic, and he found it sitting there, crumpled, roughly two years later.

He plays with a fan-made 52-card subset of the journey deck, the full one being large and diluted, and notes the game famously shipped with no box at all — in a burlap sack. He built one himself from an old game and a scanned cover.

----

Daniel calls this more party management than heroics, and doesn't mind. When does managing a party stop feeling like being one?
